title: I used claude to build me a free survival game on Itch- Blade and Branch Trailer
author: BladenBranch
selftext:
Hello everyone! I created this game, Blade and Branch, using entirely claude code and Meshy. I didn't touch a single aspect of it myself and mostly did it through mobile while I was at work. I made the game completely free on Itch as a result of this, and I'm honestly just not willing to market it much more than this reddit post lol. If people want to play, they can, if not, oh well. I find it very fun.

I used Opus 5.5 for pretty much everything, including prompting Meshy for new models as the ones claude initially made looked like turds, literally. A troll was a giant walking turd that it for some reason gave it a tail, but on the front of its body.

Fable 5.2 has helped me work through all of the 3D animations and improve them to a point I find ALMOST satisfactory, still lots of wonky animations.

This is an open world survival game with randomized maps all built with geography in mind, warmer climates near equators, mountains along fault lines, a world that wraps around horizontally with a giant ice wall blocking the north and south. Blade and branch is a brutal English folklore survival where literally anything could potentially kill you, and there's very few ways to see how difficult an enemy is, so you must learn through experience. I'd say with what the game has so far it has the depth and potential for hundreds of hours, and it's also co-op with friends if you use hamachi or Tailscale.

If you have any questions about the workflow i used to achieve this please ask away!

Here is the Itch link if you're interested in checking it out: [https://bladeandbranch.itch.io/blade-and-branch](https://bladeandbranch.itch.io/blade-and-branch)

comments.body: looks pretty sick dude! reminds of valheim with a different camera angle

replies.author: BladenBranch
replies.body: I got a lot of inspiration from current survivals like Valheim and Dragonwilds but the biggest inspiration was a game called Haven and Hearth which I've played for literally almost 15 years of my life. HnH just has open world permadeath pvp so it's riddled with griefers and such that kill the playerbase to sub 200 every world. I did add a permadeath option to this but with a reincarnation mechanic that returns you with 50% of previous stats and xp boost back to where you died at. Try it out and let me know what you think! It's pretty fun with friends!
